brief: BofA's weekly economic note argues the Fed's September hike, as expected and hawkish, supports its call for two more 25bp increases in October and December (75bp total cycle), while markets pricing closer to 100bp are overpricing the cycle, especially for the ECB, BoE and BoC given initial conditions different from the post-COVID recovery. Underlying US inflation is stuck near 2.5%, and nominal spending above the 5% threshold historically linked to inflation overshoot keeps hike risk skewed higher, though a persistent oil shock could force the Fed to choose between an inflation overshoot and a hard landing. In Europe, euro area corporate health fell into its most vulnerable position since 2022 on tighter financing, with SMEs facing a widening credit gap even as large-firm access improved. The BoE held rates but turned more hawkish, and BofA now sees a November hike as a possible new base case if energy prices persist, though it still views market pricing of near-four hikes as excessive. Separately: Mexico's investment-grade rating is at risk absent faster growth, Kenya's opposition remains fragmented ahead of elections, and El Niño threatens Australian/NZ food prices and growth without lifting headline inflation.
